messages: Maria (Marketing): Hey design — we need a compact asset pack for an upcoming launch + webinar on inference economics. Main asks: 1) single-slide benchmark explainer diagram (SVG + PNG export), 2) three social assets (square + wide + story), 3) one-page inbound lead routing microflow (PDF + PNG), and 4) a small hero GIF for the landing page. Deadline: assets final by 2026-04-08 so we can integrate into email and webinar pages. Figma file: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/redwood-marketing-launch (see page 'inference-econ / assets'). Please confirm availability. :calendar:
messages_note_1: Kevin (Design Lead): @Maria (Marketing) available — should be doable. Quick clarifying q's: a) Is the benchmark explainer more visual (diagram + sparkline) or data-first (table + annotations)? b) Routing microflow: do you want a simplified 3-step diagram (lead -> qualification -> nurture) or a full swimlane with tech touchpoints (Webhook, HubSpot, Webhook auth)?
messages_note_2: Maria (Marketing): Go visual-first with a single hero diagram — high-level latency vs cost sparkline + annotated callouts (batching, KV cache, fallback). For microflow: need swimlane with 3 lanes: inbound -> routing rules -> GTM handoff (we route by intent -> model cost tier -> AE/SDR). Include short labels for integration points (API, webhook, HubSpot). Avoid platform internals. Also please include a small PNG export sized 940x540 for the webinar hero.
messages_note_3: Liam (Product): Adding product context — callout copy for the benchmark slide should include one-line: 'Optimize inference cost without sacrificing latency' and a tiny stat if we can: 'up to 3x cost reduction vs naive serving' (we'll QA numbers with research later). Also we'll need an editable SVG so sales can tweak minor copy. :memo:
messages_note_4: Kevin (Design Lead): Got it. Priorities sorted. Palette/brand: @Priya (Brand Ops) any guardrails re: new sparkline color or motion? We want to avoid green-to-red gradients that imply quality issues. Also legal asked to avoid explicit competitor callouts.
messages_note_5: Priya (Brand Ops): Thanks @Kevin. Brand rules: use primary Redwood blue (#0057D9) and the accent amber from the launch kit only for highlights. Motion: subtle 300ms easing, loop once then stop. No competitor logos or comparative bars with named rivals. For localization: provide source text in a separate layer in Figma and keep type sizes flexible for German/French. Also add an accessibility note: 4.5:1 contrast minimum for key CTAs.
messages_note_6: Kevin (Design Lead): Copying checklist -> I'll: a) build master artboard with export presets (SVG, PNG 940x540, 1200x1200, 1200x628), b) include a 'copy layer' for translations, c) attach a 3-frame GIF for hero (compressed). ETA: first mockups by 2026-03-31, final by 2026-04-07. Tagging FigmaBot to create export presets.
messages_note_7: FigmaBot: Export presets created in file 'redwood-marketing-launch' — slices: hero_940x540, social_1200x1200, social_1200x628, microflow_pdf. Exports will be available under Team > Exports after first save.
messages_note_8: Maria (Marketing): Amazing — appreciate the timeline. A couple small asks: - Please add a tiny caption line for the webinar registration CTA: 'Register — limited seats' (use small uppercase). - Make sure the sparkline annotation calls out 'prefix caching' and 'quantization' as two knobs. - Can we get one alt-variant with lighter copy for paid social?
messages_note_9: Kevin (Design Lead): Will do. For the lighter paid social variant I suggest trimming the tagline and boosting the CTA prominence. I'll drop 3 options in the Figma page 'social_variants' and mark one as 'paid-friendly'. Anything else?
messages_note_10: Priya (Brand Ops): One last note — when you export SVGs, set shapes to outlines and avoid embedded fonts for partner use. I'll run legal/branding sweep once Kevin posts final exports. :white_check_mark:
messages_note_11: Maria (Marketing): Perfect. Thanks team. I'll queue the assets with comms and add the webinar registration link once landing page is live. Ping me in-thread with the mock files. :rocket:
